key.formula: ladder inversion (probit fit): for each (line, P_over) keep P_under = 1 - P_over with 0.005 < P_under < 0.995; z = norm_inv(P_under) = Phi^-1(1 - P_over); fit z = slope*line + inter by least squares; slope = Sxz/Sxx; sigma = 1/slope; mu = -inter/slope; r2 = 1 - SSR/Szz
key.symbols: line = alt line; P_over = no-vig P(over) after pair normalization; sigma = the book's implicit sd; mu = the book's implicit mean; requires >= 4 usable points; returns None if Sxx <= 0 or Sxz == 0.

key.symbols: winner (mu_w, sd_w), loser (mu_l, sd_l); beta = performance noise sd (25/6 default); defaults mu0=25, sd0=25/3; dynamic factor 25/300; phi = standard normal pdf, Phi = CDF. Update order: winner updated first, then loser.

key.formula: Glicko-2: scale = 173.7178; mu = (rating-1500)/scale; phi = rd/scale; g(phi) = 1/sqrt(1 + 3*phi^2/pi^2); E = 1/(1+exp(-g(phi_opp)*(mu - mu_opp))); v = 1/sum(g^2*E*(1-E)); delta = v*sum(g*(score-E)); Illinois iteration for new volatility on f(x) = exp(x)(delta^2 - phi^2 - v - exp(x))/(2(phi^2+v+exp(x))^2) - (x-a)/tau^2, a = ln(vol^2); phi_star = sqrt(phi^2 + vol_new^2); phi_new = 1/sqrt(1/(phi_star^2) + 1/v); mu_new = mu + phi_new^2*sum(g*(score-E)); output rating = mu*scale + 1500
key.symbols: mu, phi = latent rating and rating deviation; vol = volatility; tau = 0.5 (volatility constraint); defaults rating0=1500, rd0=350, vol0=0.06; one update PER RATING PERIOD using all games in parallel (pre-period snapshot); canonical test vector A/1500 rd 200 -> 1464.06, rd 151.52.

key.formula: hierarchical Gibbs (NFL margins): y_k ~ N(eff_h - eff_a + hfa, sigma^2); eff_i ~ N(0, tau2); tau2 ~ IG(2, 50); sigma2 ~ IG(2, 50); hfa ~ N(0, 100). Conditionals: eff_t precision = 1/tau2 + games/sigma2, mean = post_var * sum_i (y - hfa + eff_opp)/sigma2 for home games and (eff_opp + hfa - y)/sigma2 for away games; hfa ~ N(s/prec, 1/prec) with prec = 1/100 + nG/sigma2, s = sum (y - (eff_h - eff_a))/sigma2; sigma2 = 1/gammavariate(a + nG/2, 1/(b + sse/2)); tau2 = 1/gammavariate(a + n/2, 1/(b + sse_t/2))
key.symbols: eff = team effect (posterior mean rating); hfa = home-field advantage; tau2 = between-team variance; sigma2 = game-noise variance; sse = residual sum of squares; sse_t = sum of squared team effects; a_ig = 2.0, b_ig = 50.0; iters=1500, burn=500 (self-test runs 800/300); seed=7. Run on nfl_games season >= 2019.

key.name: Liu-West (2001) kernel on a slow parameter
key.steps: 1) m = weighted mean of log_phi; v = weighted mean of (log_phi - m)^2. 2) h2 = 1 - a^2. 3) deterministic shrinkage: log_phi <- a*log_phi + (1-a)*m. 4) stochastic jitter: log_phi += N(0, sqrt(h2*v + 1e-8)). 5) record log_phi_var = h2*v for diagnostics.

key.name: Cornish-Fisher quantile adjustment (up to O(1/n))
key.steps: 1) term_skew = (z^2-1)*skew/6. 2) term_kurt = (z^3-3z)*excess_kurt/24. 3) if include_skew_sq: term_skew2 = -(2z^3-5z)*skew^2/36. 4) z_cf = z + term_skew + term_kurt [+ term_skew2]. A companion cornish_fisher_cdf_approx numerically root-solves the quantile map on bracket [-10, 10] and falls back to norm.cdf(x).

key.name: Deflated Sharpe gate (steps)
key.steps: Given backtest Sharpe sr, n, trials T, skew, kurt: 1) sd_sr = sqrt((1 - skew*sr + (kurt-1)/4*sr^2)/max(n-1,1)); 2) SR0 = sd_sr*[(1-gamma)*Phi^-1(1-1/T) + gamma*Phi^-1(1-1/(T*e))]; 3) DSR = Phi((sr - SR0)*sqrt(n-1)/denom); returns (P(real), SR0). 'The anti-self-deception engine: I found an edge dies here or becomes a claim.'

variants.steps: Given backtest Sharpe sr, n, trials T, skew, kurt: 1) sd_sr = sqrt((1 - skew*sr + (kurt-1)/4*sr^2)/max(n-1,1)); 2) SR0 = sd_sr*[(1-gamma)*Phi^-1(1-1/T) + gamma*Phi^-1(1-1/(T*e))]; 3) DSR = Phi((sr - SR0)*sqrt(n-1)/denom); returns (P(real), SR0). key.name: First-half market derivation from the full-game model
key.steps: 1) Take the full-game mu (= -listed_spread) and the margin sd. 2) Apply the sqrt(tau) law at tau = 0.5: h1_mu = mu/2 (i.e. S/2), h1_sd = sd*sqrt(0.5). 3) Price H1 spreads/totals with the same normal machinery; game_props also returns p_h1_home_over_half = 1 - norm_cdf(total/2 - 1.0, h1_mu + total/4, sd_t*sqrt(0.5)).

key.name: Glicko-2 (period-parallel, steps)
key.steps: 1) snapshot pre-period (mu, phi, vol) per player; 2) for each player: g(phi_opp), E, v_inv = Sum g^2 E (1-E), delta_sum = Sum g (sc - E), v = 1/v_inv, delta = v*delta_sum; 3) new volatility by Illinois algorithm (tau-bounded); 4) phi_star = sqrt(phi^2 + vol_new^2); phi_new = 1/sqrt(1/phi_star^2 + v_inv); mu_new = mu + phi_new^2*delta_sum; 5) one update per player per rating period using ALL their games.

key.name: Standalone logistic regression by IRLS (stdlib)
key.steps: 1) Prepend a bias column to X; beta = 0 with d = features + 1. 2) Iterate 25 times: eta = X*beta; p = 1/(1+exp(-eta)); W = max(p(1-p), 1e-9). 3) Gradient = X'(y - p) - ridge*beta (ridge 1e-6). 4) Hessian H = X'WX + ridge*I. 5) Solve H*delta = grad by Gaussian elimination with partial pivot (pivot floor 1e-12); beta += delta. 6) logistic_apply(beta, row) = 1/(1+exp(-X*beta)).

key.name: CVI scoring protocol (diagnostic only)
key.steps: 1) Fit parameters only on earlier games. 2) Use CVI as a residual-scale modulator (multiplies Laplace b or Gaussian σ); do not shift μ. 3) Score delta CRPS overall, and conditional CRPS on games where CVI exceeds a threshold fit on the training window. 4) Stamp DIAGNOSTIC. 5) No emission weight until the combined distribution reaches CRPS ≤ 7.099 on n ≥ 150 under the same 2,462-game filter.

key.name: Opinion pool across books/models
key.steps: 1) Clip every probability into [1e-9, 1-1e-9]; take weights (default equal). 2) method=linear -> weighted mean. 3) method=log -> weighted mean of log p and of log(1-p), then pool = exp(s)/(exp(s)+exp(s2)) (normalized odds-ratio / geometric pool). 4) method=power -> weighted mean of p^power (power = 2.0). Self-check: log pool of [0.55, 0.61] lies in (0.5, 0.62); linear pool of [0.6, 0.6] is exactly 0.6.

key.name: Devig algorithms (fair(p1, p2, method))
key.steps: 1. multiplicative: p_i/Σp (default; correct on 2-way). 2. additive: p_i − (Σp−1)/2 (equal-margin; keep for comparison). 3. power: solve p1^k + p2^k = 1 by bisection (logarithmic method). 4. Shin (1993): π_i = (1−z)p_i + z·p_i²/S, fixed-point on S, bisection on z so Σπ=1 — present but does NOT recover z on sub-1/edge books, falls back to multiplicative.

key.name: Synthetic hierarchical NB data generator with planted structure
key.steps: 1) draw team_eff ~ N(0,0.15) (n_teams), pitcher_eff ~ N(0,0.25) (n_pitchers), park_eff ~ N(0,0.20) (n_parks). 2) intercept starts at 1.6 (~5 runs). 3) per t: sample team/pitcher/park indices; eta = intercept + team_eff + pitcher_eff + park_eff; update intercept with AR 0.98*intercept + 0.02*1.6 + N(0,0.02); mu = exp(eta); p = phi/(phi+mu); y = NB(true_phi, p). 4) record true_mu and indices for audit.

key.name: Residual-target discovery loop (MOVE-37 THE method)
key.steps: 1) Fit a gradient-boosting model pre-snap. 2) Take absolute residual |y - GBM_hat| (how surprising was this play). 3) Run symbolic regression on the residual. 4) Pre-registered tournament with six kill criteria: holdout R^2, bootstrap CI vs human baseline, replication, complexity, shuffled-target null (plus dumb-baseline duel). 5) Gate: do not spend search budget unless GBM ceiling is well above R^2 ~ 0.01.

key.name: Shift vs reweight calibration test (Task F)
key.steps: Two options: Location shift - move the margin mean, keep the key-number lattice. Reweight - tilt the joint toward our moneyline and renormalize. Safe test: do both on 2019-2024, score moneyline, spread, total and team total together, and keep the one whose game-blocked interval on log loss excludes a worse fit. Do not shift until the availability model has a delta whose interval excludes 0. It does not, on the new measurement.

key.name: Venn-Abers refusal rule for moneylines
key.steps: 1) Compute exact multiprobability bounds [p0, p1] via dual isotonic regressions on the calibration set (CQR residual math on binary outcomes Y in {0,1} is invalid). 2) Width (p1 - p0) = epistemic uncertainty from data paucity. 3) Selective gate: if p1 - p0 > 0.20, refuse the pick (No-Bet). 4) Pair with Platt scaling in well-calibrated large-n environments to get precise point probabilities alongside narrow bounds for EV vs market.

key.name: Simultaneous Kelly optimizer
key.steps: 1. Maximize E[log(1+Σf_i·X_i)] over a correlated slate. 2. MC gradient ascent WITH backtracking line search (plain ascent oscillates). 3. Correlated Bernoulli slate via Cholesky decomposition + Gaussian copula (rho = latent/rank correlation); Win_i = (Φ(z_i) < p_i). 4. At ρ=0.55, optimizer prices the correlated leg to fraction 0 on its own. 5. Risk-of-ruin MC: P(hit floor), median/p5/p95 bankroll over N rounds; drawdown curve.

key.name: Laplace approximation for hierarchical NB coefficients
key.steps: 1) prior precision = inv(prior_cov + 1e-9 I). 2) minimize negative log posterior (NB loglik + Gaussian prior) with L-BFGS-B from prior mean, analytic gradient score_eta*X, maxiter 50, ftol 1e-8, eta clipped to [-20,20]. 3) numerical Hessian by finite differences on the gradient (eps=1e-5), symmetrized. 4) cov = inv(H + 1e-8 I), fallback prior_cov on LinAlgError. 5) log marginal = -nll(mode) + 0.5*(n*log(2*pi) - logdet(H)); if slogdet sign<=0, log_marg = -1e6.

key.name: CPOE construction and aggregation
key.steps: 1) For each pass attempt, a completion-probability model produces cp = P(complete | context). 2) Play-level cpoe = complete_pass - cp. 3) Aggregate to player/team level as the mean residual over attempts. 4) Use team-level rolling mean CPOE as an Elo-adjustment or spread/moneyline feature; never aggregate raw completion percentage. 5) Because play-level CPOE is a Bernoulli residual, apply shrinkage toward zero for low attempt counts (early season, backup QBs).

key.steps: Nonparametric Bayesian / MAP procedure on top of *any* pairwise model (Bradley-Terry, etc.): only declare i ≻ j when the data support it; otherwise leave a tie; agglomerative algorithm for sparse, noisy comparison graphs. key.name: Edgeworth pdf/cdf expansion up to O(1/n) with Hermite polynomials
key.steps: 1) hermite_probabilists(n, x) selects He_n explicitly for n in {0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7,9} and raises NotImplementedError otherwise (n=8 is missing). 2) pdf: phi(x) * [1 + (skew/(6 sqrt(n))) He3 + (excess_kurt/(24n)) He4 + (skew^2/(72n)) He6], each term skipped when its coefficient is below 1e-12. 3) cdf: Phi(x) minus the corresponding phi(x) He_{k-1}(x) terms (He2, He3, He5) using the integral identity. 4) quantile adjustment delegates to cornish_fisher_quantile with a first-order fallback.

key.name: Middles and arbitrage scan across two books
key.steps: 1) Take the same market from two books as (line, American price) pairs. 2) Convert both to raw implied p. 3) Arb test: if p1 + p2 < 1 a guaranteed-profit pair exists; report roi_pct = (1/(p1+p2) - 1)*100 and note stakes sized by p ratio. 4) Middle test: if the absolute line gap >= 2, compute p_hit = Phi(hi) - Phi(lo) using N((l1+l2)/2, 13.45) on the open window (floor 1e-6); report the window and p_hit. 5) Self-check: a 2-point gap on a 44/46 total must yield 0 < p_hit < 0.3.

key.name: DK DFS engine 2: tabu 1-for-1 swap portfolio
key.steps: 1) seed with greedy_leverage. 2) for up to 200 iterations: enumerate all 1-for-1 swaps against the per-position top-30 pool, keep only valid lineups, shuffle, and evaluate the first 120; skip a swap whose sorted pid tuple is in the tabu deque (maxlen 25). 3) take the best admissible swap; push the dropped-pid tuple into tabu; record (score, sorted pid key, lineup). 4) bail out every 40 iterations if the 45 s time budget is exceeded. 5) dedupe by sorted pid tuple and return the top n_keep = 10 distinct lineups.

key.name: Matrix Bernstein tail + inversion to error bars
key.steps: 1) matrix_bernstein_tail(t, d, sigma, M) = min(1, 2d exp(-t^2/2/(sigma^2 + M t/3))), returns 1.0 for t <= 0. 2) matrix_hoeffding_tail(t, d, M, n) = min(1, 2d exp(-t^2/(2 n M^2))). 3) matrix_error_bound inverts: log_term = log(2d/delta); Bernstein t = sqrt(2 sigma^2 log_term) + (M/3) log_term; Hoeffding t = sqrt(2 n M^2 log_term). 4) estimate_matrix_variance_operators builds sum A A^T and sum A^T A and takes spectral norms (ord=2). 5) noncomm_khintchine_proxy returns C*sqrt(log(d))*max(sigma_row, sigma_col) with C=2.0.

key.name: Referee scoring-environment empirical Bayes
key.steps: 1) Join officials (off_pos = R) to nfl_games and collect game totals per referee name. 2) grand = overall mean total. 3) Keep referees with n >= 80 and compute their means. 4) var_between = sum n_r*(mean_r - grand)^2 / sum n_r; sd_game = sd of all totals; avg_n = mean games per kept referee; se2 = sd_game^2/avg_n; signal_var = max(var_between - se2, 0). 5) Per referee: w = signal_var/(signal_var + sd_game^2/n_r); post = w*(mean_r - grand). 6) Report the top-5 and bottom-5 shrunk scoring environments.

key.name: IRL fourth-down utility recovery protocol
key.steps: Inverse reinforcement learning on fourth-down decisions: assume coaches maximize expected utility of a power/risk-aversion utility; estimate risk-aversion parameters (γ, α̂/β̂) from observed go/kick/punt decisions via softmax maximum likelihood, win-probability outcomes feeding the utility; logistic belief models for conversion and FG probability; real-time O(1) decision-prediction head; evaluation against the NYT 4th Down Bot-style benchmark (deepseek-move37-analysis-round-05.md §4).

key.name: Devig family — fair(p1, p2, method)
key.steps: multiplicative: p_i/Σp (the default; correct on 2-way); additive: p_i − (Σp−1)/2 (equal-margin; wrong tail behavior, keep for comparison); power: solve p1^k + p2^k = 1 by bisection (logarithmic method); Shin (1993): insider-trading model π_i = (1−z)p_i + z·p_i²/S, fixed-point on S, bisection on z so Σπ=1. STATUS: Shin present but does NOT recover z on sub-1/edge books — falls back to multiplicative. Working devigs are mult/add/power only. Do not trust Shin output z

key.name: CQR interval construction with pinball loss
key.steps: 1) Train lower/upper quantile regressors with asymmetric pinball loss at alpha_lo and alpha_hi. 2) Compute residuals on a strictly held-out calibration set as nonconformity scores E_i = max(q_lo(X_i) - Y_i, Y_i - q_hi(X_i)). 3) Take the empirical quantile of scores at rank k = ceil((n+1)(1-alpha)). 4) Inflate/deflate the bounds to guarantee coverage 1-alpha under exchangeability. 5) Ban quantile clamping: when n < ceil(1/alpha) - 1, return [-inf, +inf] or an automated No-Bet (n=5, alpha=0.10 -> k=6 > 5).

key.name: RSD — rest-deficit scale scoring (Phase 3 component)
key.steps: 1. Read home_rest, away_rest from the nflverse schedule (known pre-kickoff; no injury or stadium file needed). 2. f = |home_rest − away_rest| / 7. 3. σ' = σ·exp(β·f) with σ starting at 13.45, clipped to [8, 20]. 4. β refit every scored week on a grid from −0.30 to +0.30, on prior weeks only. 5. Missing rest would have kept σ = 13.45. 6. Refuse if Δ ≥ 0; a negative β means a larger rest gap narrows the predictive scale.

key.name: Lopez state-space fitting recipe (1701.05976)
key.steps: Public JAGS model; rewrite in PyMC/Stan. Needs historical closes + results for NFL/MLB/MLS (MLS not in paper — estimate MLS σ yourself). Risk: using the market as both feature *and* label leaks CLV. Separate a 'pure prediction' θ trained on scores from a 'market residual' model. It justifies independent per-sport models with different σ_game; gives a floor on MAE; posterior σ by sport is a principled bootstrap cap: early-season strength variance is σ²_between + σ²_within, not an ad-hoc number.

key.name: kelly2.py — portfolio Kelly + survival math
key.steps: Simultaneous Kelly: maximize E[log(1+Σf_i·X_i)] over a correlated slate; MC gradient ascent with backtracking line search (plain ascent oscillates on this objective — another hard-won lesson). Correlated Bernoulli slate: Cholesky decomposition + Gaussian copula (rho = latent/rank correlation); Win_i = (Φ(z_i) < p_i). Risk of ruin MC: P(hit floor), median/p5/p95 final bankroll over N rounds. Drawdown curve: median max-DD 72–87% at full Kelly fractions. Feller classical bound for even-money reference points

key.name: Margin-total copula joint probability
key.steps: 1) Take the marginals u = P(cover) and v = P(over) plus rho (NFL empirical 0.3-0.45; default 0.35). 2) z1 = inv(u), z2 = inv(v) (inverse normal by bisection on erf, 60 iterations). 3) Integrate the bivariate normal CDF with the 1-D midpoint rule: 120 steps from -8 to z1 of phi(t)*Phi((z2 - rho*t)/sqrt(1-rho^2)) times the step. 4) joint = integral; independent = u*v; corr_premium = joint - independent; either = u + v - joint. Self-checks: rho ~ 0 gives joint ~= 0.33 for (0.6, 0.55); rho = 0.35 gives a positive premium.

key.name: Bucketed (key-number) CRPS scoring for NFL margins
key.steps: 1) treat the residual y_resid = final_margin - close; keep mu = close as the center. 2) place discrete mass p3/2 and p7/2 at residual locations (3-close), (-3-close), (7-close), (-7-close); remaining mass cont = 1 - p3 - p7 stays continuous. 3) build the CDF on a midpoint grid lo=-60..hi=60 with n_grid=1500: F(t) = cont*Laplace_cdf(t; 0, b) + sum of discrete masses whose location <= t. 4) CRPS = h * sum_i (F(t_i) - 1{t_i >= y_resid})^2. This is the diagnostic-only variant that keeps the close as mu instead of shifting mu to a residual location.

key.name: DK DFS engine 1: greedy leverage seed builder
key.steps: 1) annotate players with mu; bucket by position sorted by -mu. 2) for tries in range(60): walk SLOTS in order; candidate list is QB-only, DST-only, or WR+RB+TE for FLEX, else the slot's position list; k = randint(0,12); scan cands[:30+k] and take the first unused player satisfying used + salary + FLOOR*(8-len(lineup)) <= CAP; otherwise fall back to the cheapest fitting candidate (note: this is the first of two identical fallback blocks in the code, so the second is dead). 3) score each complete valid 9-man lineup with gpp_score and keep the best.

key.name: NGS pressure pipeline (3 ML models)
key.steps: 1. 'Graphic neural network model (GNN)' discerns which players are blocking vs running routes and which defenders are rushing vs dropping into coverage, in real time. 2. Random forest gauges each defender's pressure likelihood in tenths of a second, plus a team composite and separate per-rusher models. 3. Blocking-matchup model identifies 'who blocked who.' 4. Pressure is called when pressure probability exceeds 75%; fully automated in the NGS pipeline; history for every pass play since 2018.

key.name: 500-signal promotion ladder (Rung law)
key.steps: 1. Signals graduate Rung 2 (predicting actual outcomes) on hundreds of thousands of play/drive labels BEFORE Rung 3 (market). 2. Intra-family weighted aggregation; family credibility W_f = baseWeight × √(k_observed/k_total). 3. Final p with shrinkage to de-vigged market: p_final = p_market + S_evidence × (p_pooled − p_market). 4. 400 abstentions → shrinks toward market. 5. The 10-month methodological correction: signals tested vs Pinnacle close for 10 months on n=2,600 was noise-vs-best-benchmark.

key.name: ladder_inverse method (verbatim, 3 steps)
key.steps: 1. american -> decimal -> raw implied p; pair-normalize over/under -> no-vig P(over). 2. Each (line, P_over) is a CDF point. P_over(line) = P(X > line). probit: z = Phi^{-1}(P_under) = Phi^{-1}(1 - P_over). 3. Fit z = (line - mu)/sigma by least squares -> mu_hat, sigma_hat + R^2. => The book's implicit mean and sd for that stat, recovered from prices. Outputs: dk_stat_distributions.csv (per player-stat: mu, sigma, hold, ladder n, R2), pinnacle_dist.csv (spread/total sigma implied by Pinnacle alt ladders), hold_xray.csv (hold by book x market type).

key.name: Mind machinery M5-M7 (portfolio + distribution + freshness)
key.steps: M5: tournament payouts are convex in outcome percentile - median-optimal lineups have no tournament edge; maximize expected ROI, not expected points ('Optimal portfolios want high-mean, high-variance, low-correlation entries; expected value is a poor objective in top-heavy tournaments'). M6: fantasy points are right-skewed (gamma) and correlated within games; single-point projections collapse the tails. M7 freshness doctrine: 'Projections lag news by design; hand-fix the stale rows before lock.' Zero-out what the news changed.

key.name: Steam and reverse-line-movement detector from snapshot diffs
key.steps: 1) Take prev and cur snapshots for one game+book ({spread, total, ts} in epoch minutes). 2) d_sp = round(cur.spread - prev.spread, 1); d_tt likewise; dt = cur.ts - prev.ts. 3) fresh = 0 < dt <= max_age_min (180). 4) Emit a steam signal for a market when |move| >= min_move (0.5) AND fresh, carrying the move and age. 5) If pct_public is supplied and the spread moved by the threshold while fresh, emit an RLM check entry with the public percentage and a note that the public-side sign must be mapped at the call site.

key.name: PSR — pressure-to-sack residual (defined, not scored)
key.steps: 1. For each defense, on strictly earlier weeks: PSR = ŝack rate − ŝack rate | pressure rate. 2. Fields: sack, qb_hit (or was_pressure once participation exists) from play-by-play, aggregated by defteam and (season, week). 3. Join only to later games; fail closed if the prior week is missing. 4. Score as σ' = σ·exp(β·PSR) with β fit on earlier games only. 5. Refuse if Δ ≥ 0. 6. It does not need depth charts; it was not scored because the play-by-play release was not pulled.

key.name: Sack/pressure split (two models, never one extrapolated sack total)
key.steps: 1) Forecast pressure generation (pass-rush win rate / STRAIN-style) from matchup features: OL vs DL grades, blitz rate, time-to-throw. 2) Forecast sack conversion conditional on pressure, driven by QB-side features (time to throw, scramble tendency, sack avoidance) and situation (down, distance, score). 3) Do not extrapolate prior-season sack totals - pressure-to-sack luck has R^2 < 0.005 with pressure level. 4) Without tracking data, mark any implementation as a proxy (nflverse pbp lacks the tracking inputs for true STRAIN).

key.name: Book-path pick scoring pipeline
key.steps: 1) Average complete two-sided implied prices across books; proportional de-vig. 2) rawEdge = fairProb - impliedProb(average chosen-side price). 3) Edge component = clamp((rawEdge+0.05)/0.10,0,1)*25. 4) Rescale edgeScore to 0-100. 5) Displayed confidence = clamped sum of consensus, depth, edge, volatility, movement, rest, form, data-quality, H2H, venue, uncertainty, cross-market and schedule-stress plus a +10 base - a heuristic market-echo composite, NOT calibrated. 6) Gate: confidence >= 70 -> PREMIUM; book-path tiers 85/80 Elite, 75/65 Strong, 65/50 Solid, else Lean.

key.name: DK DFS engine 3: field simulation + portfolio selection
key.steps: 1) simulate n lineups: seed 3 stars sampled proportional to ownership from the top-60 ownership pool, then fill remaining slots greedily with the FLOOR look-ahead; keep valid 9-man rosters as sorted pid tuples. 2) compute field percentile field_pctl = sorted total scores[int(0.995*len) - 1]. 3) build candidate lineups with greedy_leverage over lam in (0.0, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0). 4) for each k-subset of candidates compute per-lineup p_one = max(0.0005, 0.5*erfc(z/sqrt(2))) with z = (field_pctl - m)/max(v,1e-9) and v = sqrt(sum of sigma^2); p_hit = 1 - prod(1 - p_one). 5) return the subset maximizing p_hit.

key.name: Defensive-detail metric construction with computed TFL
key.steps: 1) INT forced rate per opponent dropback. 2) Forced fumble rate per play (opponent fumble == 1). 3) Opponent fumble recovery share (fumble_lost / fumble). 4) tfl_rate_per_rush is COMPUTED: nflverse pbp has no tackle_for_loss column, so every opponent designed rush with yards_gained < 0 counts as a TFL (exact by definition; will not match charting vendors' counts). 5) Takeaway rate per drive (INT or fumble+fumble_lost on pass/run). 6) Defensive TD rate per drive (return_touchdown == 1). 7) Points allowed per drive (opponent final scores / defensive drives, unfiltered sample).

key.name: Conformal CPD wrapper on existing margin (freeze at lock)
key.steps: 1. Take the numeric margin forecast per sport (NFL spread, MLB run diff, MLS goal diff). 2. Collect residuals from pre-lock, same-sport, same-season calibration games only. 3. At lock, compute pi(y_c, tau=1/2) via the conformal CPD formula. 4. Publish win probability = CPD mass on positive margin (1 - pi(0,1/2)). 5. Freeze the CPD at lock; never update conformity scores with post-lock info. 6. Block calibration windows by sport AND season (exchangeability failure mode). 7. Evaluate against closing-line implied probabilities (Brier/ECE comparable).

key.name: Concurrent idempotency claim protocol (AI invocation)
key.steps: 1. Create-or-claim the AiInvocation atomically (fields: requestFingerprint, executionOwnerToken, leaseExpiresAt, heartbeatAt, resultRef/resultHash, policyVersion). 2. Same request ID + different fingerprint -> conflict. 3. Active lease -> return IN_PROGRESS or wait; never dispatch again. 4. Stale lease -> explicit recovery/steal protocol. 5. Terminal replay returns the original validated result or a durable result reference. 6. No 'output: undefined' while reporting terminal success. 7. Attempts and funding label come from persisted original state.

key.name: Open-loop vs self-regularizing comparison harness
key.steps: 1) generate synthetic hierarchical NB sequence (T=120 default, seed 42, data seed 43). 2) construct synthetic market: p_true = logistic(true_mu-5); p_hier = 0.7*p_true + 0.3*0.5; p_mkt = clip(p_hier + N(0,0.06) - 0.03*(p_true-0.5), 0.05, 0.95) so a residual edge exists by construction. 3) open-loop: single RBPF, fixed lambda 0.25, crude model probability from particle 0's beta_mean, capital multiplied by e_frac each step. 4) self-regularizing: separate RBPF (seed+7) plus ResidualInformationEProcess(seed+7, lambda_base=0.20, info_scale=1.8). 5) return both capital paths, residual_info, ys, true_mu, market_probs.

key.name: Shin devigging (market baseline)
key.steps: 1. Reject proportional normalization (overweights favorites as lines grow extreme). 2. Shin models overround as asymmetric defense against modeled insider-trading fraction. 3. Solve quadratic for insider parameter z. 4. Disproportionately removes vig from longshots, shading fair probabilities back toward midpoint. 5. One quadratic per market (cheap). Caveat: Shin's z is not identifiable from two-way odds alone (no equation printed in the doc).

key.name: Drive-outcome second scoring model
key.steps: 1) Define a drive = one (game_id, fixed_drive) group with fixed_drive != 0; offense = majority posteam; points from score differential to capture PATs, 2-pt conversions and safeties. 2) Compute td_rate, fg_rate, punt_rate, three_and_out_rate (exactly 3 plays AND punt), turnover_drive_rate (Turnover + Opp touchdown; pick-sixes count against the offense), downs_rate, avg_drive_start_own. 3) Keep the sample deliberately UNFILTERED (punts/FGs/garbage drives are real drives). 4) Use drive-outcome distributions as a second scoring model alongside EPA (the 'drive method' margin vs the '-3 vs -7 EPA method' for BUF-DET).

key.name: NGS expected rushing yards (xRY) - The Zoo 2D CNN
key.steps: 1. Input: five vector features for all 22 players evaluated at the moment of handoff - X, Y, S (speed), A (acceleration), Dir (direction). 2. 2D convolutional neural network outputs a probability distribution over rushing outcomes (not a point estimate), scored with CRPS. 3. xRY = sum(outcome x probability). 4. Derive First Down Probability and Touchdown Probability from the same distribution. 5. Implemented in Amazon SageMaker (NGS). Winner of 2020 Big Data Bowl (2,000+ entrants).

key.name: 8 rating systems - mechanism + gotcha (ratings2.py)
key.steps: Colley (C*r=b; identical records -> identical ratings, test schedules must account); Massey (LSQ on margins, needs ridge); SRS (damped fixed-point 0.7, normalize mean 0); PageRank (edges loser->winner, weight 1+|margin|/10); Keener (MUST column-normalize, row-normalization -> uniform trap); Glicko-2 (PERIOD-PARALLEL, not sequential - sequential compounds volatility and poisons ratings; canonical vector reproduced EXACT); TrueSkill (pairwise factor-graph closed form; draws skipped); Plackett-Luce (MM; numerator = WINS). Plus ensemble_margin() averaging Colley/Massey/SRS/Keener implied margins, reporting the spread-of-views.

key.name: CLV ledger protocol (the honesty metric)
key.steps: 1) add(id, market, bet_amer, stake) when a bet is placed (records ts_add, close_amer=None, result=None). 2) close(id, close_amer) when the market closes; store clv = p(bet)/p(close) - 1. 3) settle(id, w/l/p). 4) report(): over bets with a close, mean CLV, beat-close rate = share with clv > 0, and the t-stat = mean/(sd/sqrt(n)) flagged SIGNIFICANT at |t| > 2; add settled P&L in units (win = stake*(amer/100 or 100/-amer), loss = -stake, push = 0). 5) Live wiring: snapshot Pinnacle markets/related/straight for the game when a pick is logged, re-snapshot post-kickoff, and take the last pre-cutoff price as the close.

key.name: The showdown: model vs Pinnacle close vs blended pool on a held-out season
key.steps: 1) Train on seasons 1-4 (all but 2425), test on 2425. 2) Score DC, KN (with DC lambdas), the Shin/multiplicative-devigged Pinnacle close (inv = 1/oh + 1/od + 1/oa; p = (1/o)/inv), and two fixed blends w = 0.3 and w = 0.5 of model and market probabilities. 3) Metric = per-match -log(the probability assigned to the realized result), averaged; report n for the model rows and n_mkt for the market rows (only matches with all three odds). 4) Report the DC gap vs Pinnacle in nats/match and in percent. 5) Store every fit (model, scope, params, logloss, n, timestamp) into the research.db fits table.

key.name: Prop pricing pipeline: project from EPA, price with the book's own sigma, detect edge
key.steps: 1) Project mu for the player stat from nflverse EPA / props_deep NB2. 2) Take the per-stat prior sigma from the reconstructed DK sigma table (their variance modeling is already done) or the inverted Pinnacle sigma for game markets. 3) Price with P(over) = 1 - Phi(line; mu, sigma). 4) Compare against DK's own mu_hat recovered from the devigged main line; declare the prop live when |our mu - DK mu_hat| > ~0.4*sigma. 5) Also treat DK mu_hat as a free consensus projection feed. 6) For game totals, update/blend the 13.45 constant with Pinnacle's 13.19 (sigma^2 = w*13.19^2 + (1-w)*13.45^2).

key.name: nfelo unit-rating pipeline
key.steps: 1) Decompose team performance into unit ratings (passing, rushing, special teams) using EPA from play-by-play. 2) Track unit performance with an EWMA with offseason regression and contextual game adjustments. 3) Convert unit ratings to predicted point differential vs an average team. 4) Combine units into a single Elo (EloTranslator) trained to minimize log loss on game win probability. 5) Regress the main team Elo toward market spreads to improve margin prediction; add a separate QB Elo and an SRS market-implied strength component from win-total futures. 6) Output power rankings, per-game spreads, win probabilities, EV vs market lines and full-season sims.

key.name: DFS optimizer (GSE) exact DP + leverage
key.steps: 1. Exact dynamic programming over (roster-slot fill state) x (salary bucket); provably optimal for the given objective. 2. Cash mode maximizes projection (median); GPP maximizes ceiling (open: ceiling vs top-percentile of simulated outcomes). 3. Exposure control: maxExp = 1-100% per-player cap across generated lineups; greedy rejection vs DP-integrated open. 4. leverage = ceiling / (proj * own) (correctness under question). 5. Lineup rules structure observed via SaberSim: player exposures, team stacks, game stacks.

key.name: Risk of ruin and drawdown by Monte Carlo (plus the classical Feller bound)
key.steps: 1) floor = floor_frac * bankroll (default 0.5 x 100). 2) For each of trials bankroll paths, step rounds bets: draw each bet's win at random with probability p, accumulate ret via per-unit payout b (win) / -1 (loss) times the fraction. 3) Break the path when bank <= floor and count it ruined; record the final bank. 4) Return p_ruin = ruined/trials, floor, median final bank and the p5/p95 finals. 5) drawdown_curve tracks the running peak and the max (peak - bank)/peak per path; report median/p95/worst. 6) classical_ruin_even_money(p, f, units=100) returns (q/p)^(units/f) as the closed-form reference (1.0 if p <= q).

key.name: Weather covariate OLS against real closing totals (2006-2018)
key.steps: 1) Build closes from closing_lines.csv rows where type == TOTAL, keyed by alt_game_id. 2) Pull nfl_games rows with temp IS NOT NULL, scores present, season >= 2006. 3) Skip a game when the closing total or the wind is missing. 4) X = [wind, temp - 70.0, dome (roof in dome/closed/retractable), 1.0]; y = actual_total - closing_total. 5) Solve the normal equations XtX b = Xty with a +1.0 ridge added to the diagonal (Gaussian elimination, partial pivot); k = 4. 6) R^2 = 1 - ss_res/ss_tot; SE_j = sqrt(ss_res/(n-k) * (XtX[j][j])^-1). 7) Print coefficients with standard errors and the market-residual baseline reference ~13.4/sqrt2 ~= 9.5.

key.steps: 1. Migrate fully from point probabilities to margin densities - a density prices every alternate spread/total/teaser and is the basis for pricing middles. 2. Operational gate: new density model must show CRPS improvement <0.01 on >=150 settled spreads vs widened Gaussian baseline before live execution.

key.steps: 1) read the operator's own logged-in cookie (DK_COOKIES or --cookies-file) — no auth bypass. 2) GET https://www.draftkings.com/contest/leaderboardfull/v3/contest/{contest}?page={page}&pageSize={page_size}. 3) retry up to 4 times with exponential backoff on 429/500/502/503; treat 401/403 as a fatal expired session. 4) parse JSON keys leaderBoard/entries/LeaderBoard, mapping entryId/userName/rank/points/lineup to {entry_id, user, rank, points, lineup[]}; on JSONDecodeError fall back to a regex over embedded 'lineup' arrays. 5) append to entries_{contest}.jsonl with _page and observed_at (UTC); resume by skipping pages already present; stop on an empty page; pace 0.5 + uniform(0,0.4) s.

key.name: DFS salary-cap optimizer (greedy value plus 2-swap downgrade, documented heuristic)
key.steps: 1) Cap = 50000; slots = {QB 1, RB 2, WR 3, TE 1, DST 1}. 2) Group players by position; sort each pool by projection per 1000 dollars (p[3]/max(p[2],1)) descending. 3) Fill each slot greedily from its position pool; track salary used; keep RB/WR/TE picks in a flex pool. 4) If salary > cap, repeatedly find the worst value-rate player and swap in the next cheaper same-position alternative not already in the lineup until under cap (or stop when no alternative exists). 5) Return lineup, total projection, salary, cap_left and value_rate = proj/salary*1000. Documented as typically within 1-3% of the optimal ILP solution.

key.name: Turnover decomposition (occurrence vs recovery)
key.steps: 1) Never carry raw turnover margin or interception/fumble-recovery totals forward as team features. 2) Model turnover occurrence separately: forced fumbles and interception-thrown probability from pressure, QB decision features (aggressiveness, CPOE under pressure) and play-type mix. 3) Model recovery with a flat ~50% prior (conditioned on fumble type/location if data supports it) - count forced fumbles, never recovered fumbles. 4) Build expected-turnover differential as occurrence minus league-rate expectation using the same actual-minus-expected construction as the INT-luck columns; recovery luck = recovery share minus league mean (2025: 46.3%).

key.steps: 1. Per lineup, per trial s ∈ {1..10000}: draw team shocks Z_team ~ N(0,1), game/SVI shocks Z_game ~ N(0,1), idiosyncratic player shocks ε_i ~ N(0,1). 2. key.name: Fatigue curve and market-efficiency round
key.steps: 1) Fatigue: pull EPL matches with HT and FT scores; n = matches; h1 = total first-half goals, h2 = total second-half goals; r1 = h1/n, r2 = h2/n; ratio = r2/r1; late_share = h2/(h1+h2); Poisson equal-rate test chi2 = (h1-h2)^2/(h1+h2) with p = erfc(sqrt(chi2/2)). 2) Closing-line efficiency (n = 6,830 games 2006-2018): favorite cover rate vs close with se = sqrt(0.25/n) and the 2-se efficiency verdict. 3) Favorite-longshot bias on ML closes: decile bins by implied probability, empirical win rate vs bin midpoint, then the slope regression over bins with n >= 200. 4) Physiological layer: Rothfusz heat index, altitude flight factor 1.225/rho, circadian phase residual.

key.name: B-spline steam detection (Hawkes REJECTED)
key.steps: 1. Reject Hawkes self-exciting processes on short-horizon odds archives (weeks not seasons) - fitting self-excitation on non-stationary short windows overfits high-frequency noise. 2. Replacement (parameter-free): RTS Kalman smoother strips bid-ask bounce. 3. Cubic B-spline parameterization. 4. Compute instantaneous curvature kappa(t). 5. Steam signature: extreme global maximum in kappa(t) immediately accompanied by localized deceleration dip in trajectory velocity (market maker absorbing liquidity shock).

key.name: Calibration layer hierarchy (raw score -> bettable probability -> interval)
key.steps: 1) Start from the raw model score. 2) Apply one of Platt (sigmoid(A*logit(p)+B)), temperature (sigmoid(logit(p)/T)) or beta calibration (z/(1+z), z = p^a(1-p)^b/c) fitted by NLL. 3) Wrap with split conformal: take the ceil((n+1)(1-alpha))-th smallest calibration residual as q_hat and publish the distribution-free interval. 4) For props use the asymmetric variant with separate upper/lower residual quantiles. 5) Diagnose with ECE and the per-bin reliability table; treat in-sample diagnostics as provisional until split out-of-sample. 6) Wiring note: temperature scaling is the fix for ECE 0.0538 (3 lines behind the founder gate).

key.name: Ten-facet EPA/WPA decomposition (@SamHoppen 'How the game was won')
key.steps: 1. Input: nflfastR/nflverse play-by-play. 2. Orient every play's epa/wpa to the team. 3. Assign each play to exactly one mutually exclusive facet with precedence: turnover > penalty > offense > defense > ST > Other. Ten facets: Pass Off, Run Off, Pass Def, Run Def, Takeaways, Giveaways, Off Pen, Def Pen, ST, Other. 4. Sum per facet. 5. Sanity check that WPA telescopes to final WP minus initial WP. Fully replicable from free data; only risk is the exact turnover/penalty precedence rule.

key.name: Fitted book-path calibration (regularized logistic regression)
key.steps: 1) Fit a logistic regression of pick outcome on confidence + sport + market. 2) Validate temporally (train/test split by time, not at random). 3) The fitted model beat the raw heuristic on test log-loss (0.6678 vs 0.7608); map confidence 100 to ~54% win probability rather than treating it as a probability. 4) v5.3.0 proposal: calibrated confidence via regularized logistic regression, Premium as a conjunction gate, separate sport x market calibration heads with explicit push handling, benchmark logistic vs a GBM challenger, fit thresholds from out-of-sample CLV/ROI, ship behind CALIBRATION_ADJUSTMENTS_ENABLED kill switch after backtest.

key.name: Walk-forward gate protocol (frozen filter)
key.steps: 1. Regular season only. Scored games 2017 week 1 through 2026 week 5. 2. A game counts only if home_score, away_score, and spread_line are present (no imputation). 3. μ = spread_line (positive = home favored). 4. History for any fitted scale is strictly earlier weeks, including pre-2017 regular-season games. 5. Score Gaussian(μ=spread_line, σ=13.45) with CRPS. 6. Candidate must print CRPS ≤ 7.099 with n ≥ 150. 7. Do not set passed true otherwise; content of walk_forward.json gates emission: missing/stale (>168 h)/unreadable/passed not exactly true → 0-object, no pick.create / pick.updateMany.

key.name: Decompose the gap (section E)
key.steps: Missing information: list every symbol in the equation with no point-in-time file; add a feature only if a pre-outcome file exists; do not use actual starters. key.name: ladder_inverse - Pinnacle game ladders
key.steps: 1) Glob snapshots/pinnacle_mkt_*.json (14 market trees). 2) Keep markets of type spread / total / team_total. 3) For spread, pair home/away at mirrored lines keyed by round(abs(points),1); for total/team_total key by round(points,1) with over/under designations. 4) Convert all prices to raw implied p; keep lines that have BOTH sides. 5) Pair-normalize (p_side/(p_o+p_u)) and compute per-line hold. 6) Fit the probit normal CDF to the no-vig CDF points (>= 5 lines) -> mu, sigma, R^2, n_lines; spread uses 1 - novig, totals use 1 - p_under. 7) Write pinnacle_dist.csv (matchup, market, period, mu, sigma, r2, n_lines, hold_mean); report sigma median and hold mean by market/period over R^2 >= 0.97 fits.

key.name: Locked-mean two-normal mixture fitting and scoring
key.steps: 1. Both component means locked at the close (μ = spread_line). 2. Fit weights/narrow scale on prior residuals only (coarse grid on the last 900 prior residuals for the 7.138654 run). 3. CRPS via the two-normal closed form (E|X−y| minus half E|X−X'|). 4. Land it as a diagnostic scorer on the frozen filter inside dfs/walk_forward/ using the refreshed schedule file; write its CRPS next to the Gaussian 7.154021. 5. If the harness number disagrees with 7.138654, print both and keep the harness number; do not retune the grid until the disagreement is explained. 6. Pre-register it as the candidate; selection of best-of-many on the same 2,462 games is a leak.

key.name: Cognitive SLO / autonomy error budget: downgrade triggers + hysteresis
key.steps: Each autonomy grant consumes an error budget. The system must automatically recommend or enforce a downgrade when: policy or security violations occur; error budget is exhausted; input/output distributions drift materially; model or tool version changes; evaluation coverage becomes stale; owner overturn rate rises; unexplained cost rises; a capability produces an ambiguous irreversible effect. Downgrade is automatic within current authority. Promotion is not. Hysteresis: downgrade threshold; separate higher promotion threshold; minimum observation window; cooldown after incident; mandatory fresh held-out evaluation after model/tool change.

key.name: Selection-publication validation procedure (GSE)
key.steps: 1. Raise resolution via selective publishing (Proposition 5): emit a pick only when |p - 0.5| >= delta, targeting Var[P | published] >= 0.03. 2. Choose delta on an early chronological window and evaluate it on a later one - a threshold tuned and scored on the same rows is a curve fit; report pi_delta = E[Y | published] on the held-out window alongside Var[P | published]. 3. Run both integrity instruments (e-process and calibration instruments) on the dropped set; either firing means the filter is discarding real skill.

key.name: Leakage-free expanding-window backtest with verification scoring and temperature refit
key.steps: 1) Fetch completed games for the season/weeks from the keyless ESPN scoreboard (cache data/espn_scores_<season>.json). 2) Sort by week; for each game index i require len(prior) >= 8 games to train. 3) Fit SRS on ALL prior games only (iters = 60). 4) Predict mu = srs[home] - srs[away] + hfa (2.0) and p_home = 1 - norm_cdf(0.0, mu, 13.45). 5) Score: Brier = mean((p_home - home_win)^2); CRPS = mean(crps_gaussian(mu_pred, 13.45, margin)); PIT histogram (10 bins, uniform target); pick accuracy. 6) Report the max PIT deviation from uniform (GOOD if < 0.15). 7) Temperature refit on (p_home, home_win) and report Brier before/after (improved or already calibrated).

key.name: DVOA-inspired opponent-adjusted efficiency layer
key.steps: 1) Compute per-play value over a situational league-average baseline for that down, distance and field position; value progress toward a first down rather than raw yards. 2) Adjust each play for the quality of opponent faced (iterative or regression-based strength-of-schedule correction on EPA). 3) Strip fumble luck by treating all fumbles the same whether recovered or not. 4) Early-season: regress observed efficiency toward a preseason prior with a DAVE-style decaying weight, heavier prior on defense (defense stabilizes slower); Week-1 prior-year opponent-adjustment split 50% pass offense / 30% run offense / 20% opposing defense. 5) Label the implementation DVOA-inspired, never DVOA (exact weights proprietary).

key.name: Third-degree spherical-radial Cubature Kalman Filter
key.steps: 1) generate 2n cubature points xi at +-sqrt(n)*e_i, equal weights w = 1/(2n). 2) Predict: factor P = S S^T by Cholesky (fallback: eigendecomposition with eigenvalue floor 1e-12); X = x + S xi^T (n x 2n); propagate each column through f; x_pred = w * sum of propagated columns; P_pred = Q + w * sum of outer(dx, dx); enforce symmetry P = 0.5(P+P^T). 3) Update: recompute S; Y = h on the cubature points; y_pred = w*sum Y; Pyy = R + w*sum outer(dy,dy); Pxy = w*sum outer(dx,dy); K = Pxy inv(Pyy) (pinv fallback); x = x + K(y - y_pred); P = P - K Pyy K^T, symmetrized. 4) Approximate Gaussian log-likelihood of the innovation: -0.5*(m log 2pi + logdet(Pyy) + innovation' solve(Pyy, innovation)); returns -1e6 if slogdet sign <= 0 or on LinAlgError.

key.name: Physical-plausibility gating (Rung 1)
key.steps: 1. Flag any player movement exceeding 13 m/s as fatally corrupt (not an outlier). 2. Market series: reject non-finite timestamps (SourceCannotSpeakAsOfError). 3. Scan for fixture triplication, phantom matches from API timeouts, corrupted consensus metrics (e.g., public betting percentages pinned at exactly 1.0000 across a full MLB run-line slate). 4. Wind direction must not be naively averaged (mean of 0 and 359 wrongly yields 180) - store as categorical strings or directional cosines. Design assumptions: market-data violation rate 'well above five percent'; spatial datasets 'approaching 19%' corrupt.

key.name: Lopez state-space fit and use
key.steps: 1. Observations = betting-market margins (spread/totals-implied) for NFL/MLB; MLS is not in the paper, so estimate MLS sigma yourself. 2. Nested AR(1) team strength: between-season variance sigma^2_B, within-season week variance sigma^2_W, game observation noise sigma^2_G; constant vs team-specific HA. 3. Fit in JAGS (20k iterations / 2k burn-in / thin 5) or rewrite in PyMC v5. 4. Use sigma_G as the league-specific irreducible error; use posterior sd(theta) early in the season as confidence width. 5. Use the market reliability plot as the CLV/calibration reference GSE must beat or match. 6. Split the observation: scores for talent, closes only for evaluation (avoid line-as-feature-and-label leakage).

key.name: NGS tackle probability pipeline
key.steps: 1. Frame-level labeling; compute tackle probability for every player during each play every 10th of a second. 2. 20 features per frame for all 11 defenders; >2 million data points. 3. Trained on 2018-2022, tested on 2023; 15 different ML models tested on >1M data points in 4 months. 4. Production in <6 months; real-time inference through hundreds of thousands of data points per second, millions per game. 5. Fuse tackle probability + expected yards models -> 'tackle yards saved'. 6. Derived metrics: missed tackles by defender; tackle efficiency; missed tackles forced; group tackles; open-field tackle attempts; missed-tackle yards lost; tackle yards saved.

key.name: Pick'em payout-table engine (structural hold, breakeven, correlation sensitivity)
key.steps: 1) Encode the public payout tables POWER and FLEX. 2) Compute EV per unit at per-leg p: power_ev(n,p) = POWER[n]*p^n; flex_ev(n,p) = sum_k FLEX[n][k]*binom(k,n,p). 3) hold = 1 - EV. 4) Solve the breakeven per-leg probability by 60-step bisection where EV = 1.0 (EV increasing in p). 5) Correlation sensitivity: simulate P(all n legs hit) with an equicorrelated Gaussian copula (threshold z* solving Phi(z*) = p, then z_i = sqrt(rho)*f + sqrt(1-rho)*g_i), n_sims = 30000, and recompute EV = POWER[n]*P(all). 6) Sweep per-leg p = 0.50/0.52/0.54 to show hold shifting; the mechanic: lines engineered toward p ~ 0.5, hold structural, edges only where per-leg p beats breakeven AND correlation favors the player.

key.name: calibration2.py — calibration layer
key.steps: Platt scaling (1999): p_cal = σ(A·logit(p_raw)+B), gradient descent on NLL. Temperature scaling (Guo 2017): p_cal = σ(logit(p_raw)/T), bisection on NLL. Beta calibration (Kull/Filho/Flach 2017): 3-param monotone map m(p) = 1/(1+1/((p^a(1−p)^b)/c)); identity = (1,1,1). Split conformal (Vovk/Papadopoulos): interval ŷ ± q̂ where q̂ = ⌈(n+1)(1−α)⌉-th smallest calibration residual; distribution-free coverage ≥ 1−α under exchangeability. Conformal prop intervals — asymmetric (separate over/under residual quantiles) for prop pricing. ECE + reliability table — expected calibration error with per-bin conf-vs-acc. recalibrate_report — fits all three, reports Brier before/after

key.name: Phase-entropy + vorticity diagnostic on a spectral velocity field
key.steps: 1) project U, V, W to divergence-free and zero the (0,0,0) mode; apply the 2/3-style dealias mask. 2) phase_entropy: power = |U|^2+|V|^2+|W|^2, mask power > 1e-18, normalize, S_spec = -sum p log p; theta = angle(U+V+W), R = |sum p exp(i theta)|; S_phase = entropy of the 16-bin power-weighted histogram over (-pi, pi) after dropping zero bins. 3) direction_curvature: vorticity from curl in Fourier space; wmax = max |omega|; hi = |omega| > 0.5*wmax; compute ||grad xi||_inf on hi from the unit-vorticity direction field; form the strain tensor S = 0.5(G+G^T) from the velocity gradient tensor and D = (omega . S omega)/(|omega|^2 |S|), averaged over hi. 4) time integration: RK2 (Heun) with spectral advection and NU*ksq diffusion, re-projected each step.

key.name: Credits-aware multi-provider LLM routing with a JSON ledger
key.steps: 1) provider resolution: CLAUDE_PROVIDER env in {bedrock, anthropic, auto}; auto prefers bedrock when AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are set, else anthropic. 2) Bedrock path uses boto3 bedrock-runtime invoke_model with anthropic_version 'bedrock-2023-05-31' and a mapped model id. 3) Anthropic path uses the anthropic SDK messages.create. 4) on any primary-provider exception, log a warning and fall back to Anthropic direct. 5) estimate cost from the token counts with a rough per-million price table and append a CreditUsage row (provider, model, tokens, estimated_cost_usd, timestamp, request_id, credit_pool) to the JSON ledger, updating per-pool totals. credit_pool is hardcoded 'aws_activate' for Bedrock and 'anthropic_startup' for direct.

key.name: Mind data contracts (thought / investigation / update)
key.steps: Thought = one JSON line: {"id":"t-...","ts":...,"paper_path":...,"equation_latex":...,"claim":...,"domain":...,"prediction":...,"kill_test":{"metric":...,"threshold":...,"n_min":0},"status":"queued"}. A thought with no paper_path (local path or URL) is dropped. Investigation = a thought with status=queued bound to one runner: compute (Python on files on disk), challenge (second model must emit same normalized equation string), measure (metric on a replayable table with a timestamp rule). Mind update = appended line: {"thought_id":...,"metric":...,"n":...,"value":...,"ci":[null,null],"killed":false,"receipt_path":...}; if killed is true the index row status becomes KILLED; the equation can remain as a signal - it is not an edge.

key.name: Hierarchical Gibbs sampling for team ratings, HFA, and variance components
key.steps: 1) Load home/away/margin rows for season >= 2019. 2) Build the per-team game list (side, opponent, margin). 3) Initialise eff = 0, hfa = 2.0, sigma2 = 100.0, tau2 = 25.0 with IG(2, 50) priors and hfa ~ N(0, 100). 4) Each iteration: draw each team effect from its normal conditional (precision 1/tau2 + n_games/sigma2; mean = post_var * sum of (y - hfa + eff_opp)/sigma2 for home games and (eff_opp + hfa - y)/sigma2 for away games); draw hfa; draw sigma2 from the inverse-gamma using the residual sum of squares; draw tau2 from the inverse-gamma using the sum of squared team effects. 5) Discard the burn-in (500 of 1,500 iterations), keep draws. 6) Report posterior mean sqrt(tau2) (team spread), sqrt(sigma2) (game noise), hfa with a 95% CI, and the top/bottom posterior team means.

key.name: Clean market-efficiency round (Shin-devigged FLB plus hygiene check, plus temperature dose-response)
key.steps: 1) Build 2-way ML closes from closing_lines.csv (require exactly 2 sides) and join results. 2) Convert both prices to raw implied; run shin_devig_nway to get fair probabilities. 3) Bin by fair probability decile b = min(9, int(pf*10)); accumulate wins and counts; print edge = emp - mid per bin. 4) Collect every game in bin 0 as the hygiene list; print the wins with game id, side, American price and fair probability, and the |odds| range and median to distinguish real longshots from data errors. 5) Regress empirical win rate on bin midpoints over bins with n >= 200 for the FLB slope (<1 = longshots overpriced). 6) Temperature dose-response: bin (actual_total - closing_total) by temperature bands (<32, 32-39, 40-59, 60-74, 75-84, 85+) and print mean residual, se and t.

key.name: Residual-information self-regularizing fractional e-process (one step)
key.steps: 1) rbpf.update(y, extra_features) first (causal). 2) model_prob_over: if not supplied, uses a placeholder logistic on the clipped model mean, P = 1/(1+exp(-(mean_mu - 5.0))). 3) I_res = estimate_residual_information(p_model, m_market, hierarchical_mean_prob) = |logit(p)-0.5*(logit(m)+logit(h))| * (1-exp(-|logit(p)-logit(h)|)), clipped to [0,5]. 4) drawdown dd = 1 - capital/peak_capital. 5) lambda = clip(lambda_base*(1+info_scale*I_res)*exp(-2*dd), min_lambda, max_lambda). 6) temperature = temperature_base*(1+0.5*I_res) (computed, and the comment says it could be fed back into RBPF prior variances, but in this code it is returned only and never applied). 7) e_raw = binary LR on outcome = 1 if y > 5 else 0 (placeholder line). 8) e_frac = 1 + lambda*(e_raw-1). 9) capital *= e_frac; log_capital = log(capital + 1e-300); peak_capital updated.

key.name: Karlis-Ntzoufras bivariate Poisson EM (league-level and team-level)
key.steps: 1) Optional decay weights w_i = exp(-ln2/half_life_days * days_from_max_date). 2) Initialise lam1 = weighted mean x - 0.15, lam2 = weighted mean y - 0.15 (floor 0.05), lam3 = 0.3. 3) E-step: for each match compute the posterior E[k] = sum_k k*Pois(k;lam3)*Pois(x-k;lam1)*Pois(y-k;lam2) / sum_k Pois(k;lam3)*Pois(x-k;lam1)*Pois(y-k;lam2) over k = 0..min(x,y). 4) M-step: lam1 = sum w*(x - E[k])/sum w, lam2 = sum w*(y - E[k])/sum w, lam3 = sum w*E[k]/sum w with floors 0.02/0.02/0.001. 5) Repeat 80 iterations. 6) Team-level variant kn_team_lambda3 takes the DC per-match marginals (lam_h, lam_a) and EM-fits only the shared component lam3 (init 0.2, floor 1e-4, 40 iterations) - the test is whether lam3 survives once team means are in. 7) Evaluate with kn_loglik_matches: per-match log of sum_k Pois(k;lam3)*Pois(x-k;lam_h-lam3)*Pois(y-k;lam_a-lam3).

key.name: Hardened Rao-Blackwellized particle filter for hierarchical NB totals (one sequential update)
key.steps: 1) per particle i: _predict_discrete draws fresh team/pitcher/umpire/park indices with sticky probabilities 0.15/0.25/0.10/0.05. 2) _ckf_time_update inflates beta_cov by Q_scale*I (0.01) and symmetrizes (full CKF predict is NOT wired). 3) _build_design makes X of length n_beta=4: x[0]=1 intercept, x[1]=team_idx/n_teams-0.5, x[2]=pitcher_idx/n_pitchers-0.5, x[3]=park_idx/n_parks-0.5, extra features padded into slots 4+. 4) phi = exp(clip(log_phi,-2,5)); laplace_approx_nb(y, X, phi, prior_mean, prior_cov) returns (mode, cov, log_marg) from the external negative_binomial_laplace module. 5) beta_mean <- mode, beta_cov <- cov (Rao-Blackwellized analytic posterior). 6) p.log_weight += log_marg. 7) normalize weights in log space via max-log-sum-exp; ESS = 1/sum(w^2). 8) if ESS < 0.4*N: systematic resampling, then Liu-West kernel with a=0.98 on log_phi. 9) return ess, mean_beta (weighted), mean_phi, max_weight.

key.name: CEPT four-expert multiplicative-weight ensemble + lock rule
key.steps: 1. Expert 1 sport generative score (MLS: Poisson/Dixon-Coles/1906.05029 pre-game slice; NFL: Gaussian margin or Lopez state-space; MLB: run model, COM-Poisson 2409.17129 if overdispersed); e-value = likelihood ratio of settled outcome density vs closing-line implied density (the control measure). 2. Expert 2 market/CLV = the close itself (e-value ~1; prevents the ensemble wandering from a calibrated price). 3. Expert 3 conformal / partial-rank conservative p (ties mapped to 0.5+eps). 4. Expert 4 intervention residual: recompute the pick with (a) market features dropped and (b) injury/news features dropped; if the sign flips, emit e=1 (abstain) or a downweighted p. 5. Update w_t^(k) proportional to w_{t-1}^(k) * e_t^(k); ensemble wealth W_t per formula. 6. Lock only when: wealth growth on the last calibration window >= 1, Expert 3's interval excludes 0.5 (or CLV edge >= threshold), and Expert 4 does not abstain.

key.name: Gate sequence / refusal-certificate protocol
key.steps: Gates are sequential and Gate n+1 does not open unless gate n returned PASS, FAIL or TURNED_AWAY with a reason; a skipped gate fails the run. Gate 0 emits a refusal certificate (set_of_equations_finite, zfc_theorems_recursive, list_is_decision_procedure, copyright_fence, arxiv_crawl_fence, worktree_fence, context_fence, terminal) and terminal must be TURNED_AWAY. Gate 1 quotes live catalog sentences. Gate 2 is the MinHash false-merge argument. Gate 3 is SimHash separately. Gate 4 pulls multi-step printed equations (Glicko-2, Bradley-Terry, Elo, TrueSkill, conformal, scoring rules, football models) with per-step objects. Gate 5 is the dedup pipeline. Gate 6 is the unrun negative control. Gate 7 is the budget trap. Gate 8 is the exit block with a fixed key list. Equation objects require name, printed_form, source_url, page_or_eq_number, verbatim_span, domain, how_to_use, null_case, non_claim, status; a span ending on '=', '\text{' or a bare backslash is REFUSED_TRUNCATED.

key.name: Off-field context build and OLS (travel, timezone, altitude, rest, short week, dome)
key.steps: 1) Load the hardcoded 32-franchise table (lat, lon, tz offset vs ET, stadium altitude ft) plus legacy abbreviations (OAK, SD, STL, WSH, LA, PHX, LAC-). 2) For every nfl_game compute travel = haversine(away city, home city) with R = 3958.8 miles, tz_shift = tz_home - tz_away, altitude_diff = alt_home - alt_away, rest_diff = away_rest - home_rest, short_week = away_rest <= 5, dome from the roof string. 3) Write nfl_context (game_id primary key) and report unmatched team abbreviations. 4) Fit OLS on resid = margin + home_spread with X = [min(travel,2500), tz_shift, min(|alt_diff|,5000)*sign(alt_diff)/1000, rest_diff, short_week_away, dome, 1.0]; k = 7. 5) SEs from the inverse diagonal of XtX (Gaussian elimination with back-substitution); print t-stats with |t| > 2 / > 1.65 stars. 6) Separately build the officials table from officials.csv keyed game_id and run the per-referee empirical-Bayes shrinkage on game totals for off_pos == R with n >= 80.

key.name: Simultaneous Kelly over a correlated slate (projected MC gradient ascent)
key.steps: 1) Build the correlation matrix rho (n x n) for the slate and Cholesky-factor it (Cholesky-Banachiewicz, floor 1e-12 on the diagonal). 2) Simulate n_sims correlated Bernoulli slates via the Gaussian copula: x ~ N(0,I), z = L x, win_i = norm_cdf(z_i) < p_i; per-sim multiplier m_i = +b_i on win else -1. 3) growth(f) = mean over sims of log(1 + sum_i f_i*m_i) (floor log(1e-9) if wealth <= 0). 4) Initialise f at naive per-bet Kelly f_i = max((b_i*p_i - (1-p_i))/b_i, 0), rescale to sum <= cap. 5) Numerical gradient with eps = 0.0025 per coordinate; trial step size lr with up to 6 backtracks (halving), project the candidate to f >= 0 and sum f <= cap, accept if growth improves by > 1e-7, then multiply the learning rate by 1.3 (capped at 1.0); stop after iters steps or when the step < 1e-4 with no improvement. 6) Return optimized fractions, growth/round, the naive uncapped Kelly fractions and naive growth for the comparison (naive overweights the correlated slate).

key.steps: Replace three rule-based enrichers with measured data from persisted NextGenStat table: Gap 1 per-defender route coverage -> use measured avgCushion + avgSeparation per receiver-week joined to opponent by schedule; name features coverage_exposure_*, never per_defender_* (exposure, not assignment). Governing rule: an absent source is closed by acquiring data, finding a cleared source, or letting the row stay absent - never by default/heuristic profile/matrix.

key.name: Eight rating systems implementation notes (ratings2.py)
key.steps: 1. Colley: solve C·r = b (C_ii = 2+n_i, C_ij = −n_ij, b_i = 1+(w−l)/2); pure algebra, no margins. 2. Massey: LSQ on point margins M·r = p; needs ridge. 3. SRS: rating_i = avg_margin_i + avg(opp rating), damped fixed-point (damping 0.7), normalize mean 0. 4. PageRank: beat-graph, edges loser→winner, weight 1+|margin|/10, iterate s = Aᵀ·s. 5. Glicko-2: PERIOD-PARALLEL Bayesian update + Illinois volatility — collect all games per player FIRST, then one update; verified vs Glickman canonical example (1464.06, 151.52, 0.05999) EXACT. 7. TrueSkill: pairwise c = √(2β²+σw²+σl²), v/w updates; draws skipped in the pairwise shortcut. 8. Plackett-Luce: MM iteration π_t = wins_t / Σ 1/(π_t+π_o); numerator = WINS. key.name: Verifier harness (frozen holdouts, scorecard, duel, joint, factgraph)
key.steps: 1) holdout.ts exports two frozen splits as constants (PICKS-H1 and NFL-H2) that are never edited without a new ID. 2) scorecard.ts computes Brier + log-loss of a candidate vs marketFairProb on identical rows, paired bootstrap P(better), per-sport strata and Wilson intervals; output is one JSON plus one markdown table. 3) joint.ts runs the one-factor-at-a-time logistic-on-market-logit test with holdout delta Brier, P(better) and the era-sign check. 4) duel.ts scores a candidate against the market-anchored baseline on PICKS-H1 - the precondition for any MODEL_VERSION bump. 5) factgraph.ts reads docs/factors/*.yaml, validates the pre-registration order, writes docs/factors/INDEX.md and the mint-log entry for every held pick, replacing gate_decisions. 6) Gate: npm run verify:holdout re-grades v5.0.0 -> v5.2.7 and ALL must score worse than the market on PICKS-H1 or the harness itself is wrong. 7) No new dependencies; stats ported from the Python reference implementations with hand-computed pins.

key.name: ladder_inverse - reconstruct DK internal mu/sigma from public prices
key.steps: 1) Load the band ladder file snapshots/dk_week6_ladders_<date>.tsv; parse the milestone threshold (points or side field, plus sign stripped) and convert American odds to raw implied p. 2) Load the main board snapshots/dk_week6_props_<date>.tsv; keep rows whose subId is in MAIN2STAT and whose side is over/under; record p_over, p_under and the line tagged MainPointLine. 3) For each (event, subId, player) band ladder take (threshold t, P_over) pairs with 0.004 < P_over < 0.996 and require >= 5 points. 4) Fit z = a + b*t by least squares on z = norm_inv(P_over); reject if sxx <= 0 or b >= 0 (P(X>=t) must decrease in t). 5) sigma = -1/b (vig-immune: the slope does not depend on the hold). 6) Anchor mu from the devigged main pair: p_over_devig = p_over/(p_over+p_under), mu = main_line - sigma*norm_inv(1 - p_over_devig); record hold = 1 - 1/(1/p_over + 1/p_under). 7) Write per-player-stat mu, sigma, ladder n, R^2 and DK's displayed baseline to dk_stat_distributions.csv; report sigma median by stat over rows with R^2 >= 0.97.

key.name: Dixon-Coles time-decay fit with grid search over xi and rho
key.steps: 1) Load epl_matches (season, date, home, away, fthg, ftag, Pinnacle close odds) ordered by date. 2) For each xi in (0.0, 0.002, 0.005, 0.01) set weights w_i = exp(-xi*days_from_max_date). 3) Initialise attack/defense from weighted goals for/against per team divided by the weighted league goals-per-team-per-match (floor 0.05). 4) 40 coordinate-ascent iterations: update each team's attack from Poisson score equations with the defense and mu held fixed; update each defense likewise (lambda_opp uses att_opp + deff_t when t is home and mu + att_opp + deff_t when t is away); update mu = log(weighted scored goals / weighted expected); clamp att/deff to +/-4 and mu to +/-2; re-center attacks to mean 0. 5) For each rho in (-0.08, -0.05, -0.02, 0.0) score the decay-normalized weighted log-likelihood (sum w*log(tau*Pois*Pois)/sum w) and keep the (xi, rho) with the highest ll. 6) Report home advantage as exp(mu) and the top attack+defense teams. 7) On the held-out season build dc_probs on an 8x8 grid; promoted/unseen teams get att = deff = 0.

key.name: props_deep.py — distributional prop models
key.steps: Negative binomial for overdispersed counts (method-of-moments fit r = m²/(v−m), p = m/v). Karlis-Ntzoufras bivariate Poisson: X=W1+W3, Y=W2+W3, shared component λ₃ = the correlation; P(X=x,Y=y) = e^{−Σλ}·Σ_k λ1^{x−k}/(x−k)!·λ2^{y−k}/(y−k)!·λ3^k/k! (verified vs brute-force enumeration: 0.1231 exact; fitting λ₃ from data: bench). Truncated normal for bounded props (completion %, FG %): P(over) within hard [lo,hi] bounds. Gaussian copula joint via MC with copula link. Bayes hierarchical shrinkage on projections: proj = w·player_avg + (1−w)·league_avg, w = n/(n + σ²_obs/σ²_prior) — early-season stats shrink HARD (the empirical-Bayes cure for small-sample hero worship). Correlated-Kelly portfolio with correlation penalty per leg. CVaR framing (Rockafellar-Uryasev) for tail-aware budget allocation. Team-total split: (game_total ± mu_margin)/2 with the corrected spread convention (the original (T+spread)/2 made the favorite score LESS — a real sign error caught by the packet)

key.name: Fail-closed printed-equation recovery from dirty rows
key.steps: 1) reject JUNK on the alias/JSX/code gate (type X = {, canonicalHistoryStatus=..., 'Add the ternary', className=, entityId=, style={{, pick={, </, />, --[a-z], var(--, href=, =>, or a leading const/function/import/export/return/class). 2) reject TRUNCATED on an empty right-hand side (TRUNC_LEFT / trailing '=' with unbalanced delimiters), a leading ellipsis, a dangling partial, or an unbalanced brace count after removing LaTeX sizing delimiters. 3) EQ_SPAN finds '<symbol-start> ... = <rest-of-line>'; the equation is the verbatim span with PROSE_CUT truncation at ', with|where|for|if|when|which|that'. 4) widen to span.end() if the extracted span is unbalanced; reject if still unbalanced, or ending on '...', a bare partial sign, END_CUT (=, backslash-text, backslash-mathrm, backslash-operatorname, backslash), or TRUNC_LEFT. 5) reject if no operator from the set =+-*/^<>≤≥≠≈∑∏∫ appears. 6) drain_row drops rows with no path/source_path and emits {equation, path, page, status: AGREE_RECOVERED, verbatim: equation in printed}; write_drain dedupes on (path, equation) and counts junk/truncated/dups/jsx_dropped.

key.name: CEPT ensemble — concrete proposal (four e-variables)
key.steps: Put four e-variables whose product is the ensemble wealth process: Expert 1 — sport-specific generative score (MLS: Poisson / Dixon-Coles / 1906.05029 pre-game slice; NFL: Gaussian margin or Lopez state-space; MLB: run model, Poisson/COM-Poisson if overdispersed); e-value = likelihood ratio of predicted outcome density vs a control measure (the closing-line implied density, C4). Expert 2 — Market / CLV expert (the close itself; e-value usually ~1; exists so the ensemble cannot wander far from a calibrated market without paying wealth — the 'humility prior'). Expert 3 — Conformal / partial-rank uncertainty expert (emits a conservative p; partial-rank ties mapped to p=0.5+ε; shines when Expert 1 is over-sharp and loses Brier). Expert 4 — Intervention residual expert (before lock compute pick under two interventions: (a) drop market features, (b) drop injury/news features; if the sign flips, Expert 4 outputs e=1 abstain or a downweighted p). Lock rule (C6): lock when (i) W_t growth on the last calibration window is ≥ 1, (ii) Expert 3's interval excludes 0.5 *or* CLV edge ≥ threshold, (iii) Expert 4 does not abstain.

key.name: NGS QB passing score - TCN + MLP + spliced binned-Pareto
key.steps: 1. Data: updates every 100 ms from RFID chips in shoulder pads. 2. Build per-timestep matrix: x/y position, x/y speed, x/y acceleration, direction, body orientation per player -> 176 columns (22 players x 8 features) x variable rows (snap to QB release). 3. Engineered extras (e.g., number of defenders within a 2-yard radius of target receiver); static play attributes (down, score, games remaining). 4. TCN encodes each player's time series (variable length, long-range temporal relations); concatenate with static features -> MLP -> spliced binned-Pareto distribution: discrete binned base capturing asymmetry/multimodality with lower tail below the 5th quantile and upper tail above the 95th quantile replaced by weighted generalized Pareto distributions from extreme-value theory, parameterized by the network. 5. Play score = rank (0-1) of actual yards gained in that play's predictive CDF, standardized; aggregate over plays. 6. AWS released PyTorch SBP code + demo notebook.

key.name: iSH / Alpine engineering lessons (transferable)
key.steps: 1. Keener needs column-normalization — row-stochastic power iteration starting at uniform STAYS at uniform. 2. Glicko-2 must be period-parallel — sequential per-game updates compound the volatility estimate (vol → 2.0+) and poison ratings; collect all games per player FIRST, then one update. 3. Gradient ascent on log-growth oscillates — needs backtracking line search (monotone improvement guarantee). 4. Plackett-Luce MM numerator = WINS, not total game appearances. 5. inv_norm bisection in MC inner loops = timeout on iSH — use random.gauss directly when the model is already Gaussian. 6. Brier reliability = bin MEAN forecast (Murphy), not bin midpoint — the packet caught this. 7. Pure-stdlib Cholesky is fine for n≤10 — no numpy needed for slate-level correlation. 8. onnxruntime has no musllinux wheels — NudeNet/NN-classifier route on iSH goes through HF Spaces (FastAPI), not local pip. 9. ESPN scoreboard API: site.api.espn.com/apis/site/v2/sports/football/nfl/scoreboard?dates=YYYY&seasontype=2&week=N — keyless, ~0.4s/game with cache. 10. Cache everything — data/espn_scores_2025.json makes the backtest re-runnable without re-hitting the API

key.name: Fourth-down decision engine (nfl4th architecture)
key.steps: 1) For a given fourth-down state estimate WP(go), WP(field goal) and WP(punt) with separate action models: go model predicts a full distribution of yards gained and includes first downs awarded by defensive penalty; punt model includes blocks, return touchdowns and fumbled returns; FG model is kick-make probability as a function of distance and roof type. 2) Feed the action-specific outcome distributions into a win-probability model (nflfastR-family WP; Baldwin 2024) with game-state inputs yardline, yards to go, score differential, time remaining, timeouts. 3) Recommend the action with the highest expected WP; the reported go boost = WP advantage of going over the best kick/punt alternative. 4) Carry documented limitations (go model excludes turnover returns; punt model ignores player identity and some penalties; FG model ignores kicker identity, outdoor weather, blocked returns) and academic corrections (Heckman-style selection-bias correction per Daly-Grafstein 2023; yardline rounding confounding per Lopez 2020; understated uncertainty per Brill-Yurko-Wyner 2023). 5) Engine use: add a fourth-down-aggressiveness team/coach feature (actual go rate vs WP-optimal go rate) and use go/punt/FG WP differentials as live situation features.

key.name: Two-stage EP model (event probabilities -> weighted sum)
key.steps: 1) Model the next scoring event within the same half as a multinomial classification over seven outcome categories from the possession team's perspective: touchdown (+7), field goal (+3), safety (+2), no score (0), opponent safety (-2), opponent field goal (-3), opponent touchdown (-7); fit six logits relative to the no-score baseline. 2) EP = probability-weighted sum of the seven point values. 3) Covariates (six): down (1-4), seconds remaining in half, yardline, log(yards to go), goal-to-go indicator, under-two-minutes indicator; plus three interactions (log(YTG)xdown, yardlinexdown, log(YTG)xgoal-to-go). 4) Observation weighting: down-weight plays by score differential and by drives-until-next-score. 5) Model selection by LOSO calibration error, not likelihood: bin predicted probabilities in 5% increments vs observed event rates and pick the model with the best leave-one-season-out calibration error. 6) Kick play overrides: two-point attempts flat 47.35% (0.947 EP); XP/FG make probability as a GAM smooth function of kick distance only, with missed-FG correction of 8 yards field position and 5.07 seconds. Validate with LOSO or drive-clustered splits, never random play splits (plays on a drive share one eventual scoring event -> label leakage).

key.name: Factor Foundry protocol (pre-registered specs, kill lines, joint-model scoring)
key.steps: 1) One YAML per hypothesis in docs/factors/<id>.yaml with id, title, hypothesis, estimand, unit, data, discover_era (<= 2019), validate_era, kill_line, mde_80pct_power, script, status in {UNTESTED, CANDIDATE, LIVE, DEAD, BLOCKED}, number, ci, n, run_sha, run_at, blocked_on. 2) The commit carrying kill_line must PRECEDE run_sha; scripts/factors/index.mjs refuses any status beyond UNTESTED/BLOCKED otherwise. 3) Score by the joint test: logistic on the market logit, add one factor at a time, report holdout delta Brier, P(better), and the discover-vs-validate sign; KEEP only if delta Brier < 0 AND P(better) >= 0.75 AND the sign agrees across eras, otherwise DEAD with the number. 4) Report every factor on the public /method/factors surface (id, hypothesis, status, validate-era number with CI and n, the kill line as written, run date); DEAD rows stay forever; LIVE rows link to the pick-card factor trail. 5) Props variant P1: target n >= 500 graded reads with kill_line and MDE written before the first read; features named before the read (usage target_share/wopr/air_yards_share, ftn_charting pressure/coverage/motion rates, low-rank player x defense interaction, career personal-best gap); score Brier vs line-implied 0.5, decile monotonicity, over-confidence above median.

key.name: ratings2.py — 8 rating systems, all verified
key.steps: Colley: solve C·r = b; C_ii = 2+n_i, C_ij = −n_ij, b_i = 1+(w−l)/2 (pure algebra, no margins; identical records → identical ratings). Massey: LSQ on point margins M·r = p (needs ridge for identifiability). SRS: rating_i = avg_margin_i + avg(opp rating), damped fixed-point (damping 0.7 stabilizes; normalize mean 0). PageRank: beat-graph, edges loser→winner, weight 1+|margin|/10, iterate s = Aᵀ·s. Keener: skew matrix S(y) = (1+y)^x/((1+y)^x+(1+1/y)^x), power iteration — MUST column-normalize (Σ_i a_ij = 1); row-normalization converges to uniform — a trap nobody documents. Glicko-2: period-parallel Bayesian update + volatility via Illinois algorithm — PERIOD-PARALLEL, not sequential (sequential per-game updates compound volatility and poison ratings); verified vs Glickman's canonical worked example: (1464.06, 151.52, 0.05999) — EXACT via rating0_map/rd0_map. TrueSkill: pairwise factor-graph closed form c=√(2β²+σw²+σl²), v/w update functions (draw handling skipped (ties) in the pairwise shortcut). Plackett-Luce: MM iteration π_t = wins_t / Σ 1/(π_t+π_o) — numerator = WINS, not total games (was a real bug). Plus ensemble_margin() — averages Colley/Massey/SRS/Keener implied margins for a matchup, reports the spread-of-views (disagreement = information)

key.name: Context Compiler v0 pipeline + acceptance gates
key.steps: Consume: #167 convergence inventory; #170 Genesis Codebase Twin and plan receipts; #171 AI call-site inventory; Git history and changed symbols; SCIP or TypeScript symbol/reference indexes; current PR graph; ownership manifest; tests and coverage relationships; decision and failure receipts; current task contract. Benchmark the current TypeScript compiler API, SCIP TypeScript indexing, Aider-style symbol/reference PageRank. Rank context by the product/quotient formula (task relevance × dependency centrality × change proximity × failure/incident relevance × ownership relevance × evidence freshness ÷ token cost). Produce: full pack; previous-pack delta; removed entries; new or changed symbols; changed assumptions; changed decisions — content-addressed so unchanged context is never re-explained; a downstream model receives the delta plus stable references when the host supports persistent context. Acceptance gates: byte-identical inputs generate byte-identical packs; pack never cites a symbol at a different blob hash; changed ownership invalidates relevant entries; token budget is never exceeded without an explicit overflow result; known load-bearing files are present in benchmark tasks; irrelevant context is measurably lower than whole-repo or flat grep baselines; model task success is equal or better with fewer tokens; the compiler records uncertainty rather than claiming completeness after parse failure.
